This dataset contains 33 transects associated with the shoreline at site nzd0001 . Each transect represents a segment of the coastline for which elevation and positional data have been analysed to estimate shoreline change trends and related metrics.

The orientation of transects spans from 313.059 ° to 359.037 °, with a mean orientation of 333.134 °, indicating the general alignment of shoreline segments within this site.

Note: Orientation data is not available for this site.

Figure 1 Site Transects

In terms of shoreline change:

  • The average linear trend across all transects is -0.009 m/year, with individual values ranging from -0.403 to 0.541 , suggesting a net erosional trend overall.

  • The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of the trend model averages 15.21 m, indicating the typical deviation between observed points and the fitted trend line.

Note: Trend analysis data is not available for this site. This may indicate insufficient temporal data for trend calculations.

Confidence intervals on shoreline position trends are also available:

  • The mean lower bound is 0.068 , and the mean upper bound is 0.11 , reflecting the uncertainty range around trend estimates.

The number of valid data points per transect ( n_points_nonan ) ranges from 150 to 185 , with an average of 176.636 .

Site Zone Analysis

Site Zone Configuration

No areas of interest (AOIs) were identified for this site. This may be due to the min_zone_length ( ) parameter being set too high, or the transect data not meeting the criteria for any defined zones.

This site has been divided in to 4 zones consisting of at minimum 3 transects each. To increase or decrease the sensitivity of the zone definitions (i.e. the number of transects required to define a zone), you can adjust the min_zone_length parameter in the run_narrative_zoning function call above. Zone definitions are customisable, and extensible, and can be modified and extended by editing the aoi_definitions dictionary in the run_narrative_zoning function call above. Time Delimited Analysis

From to

Data Processing

The analysis began with the complete satellite-derived shoreline dataset containing observations for shore-normal transects. After applying the specified date range filter from to , the dataset was reduced to observations for shore-normal transects.

These observations span years, with an average of data points per transect. The time-bounded analysis reveals an average shoreline change rate of meters per year across all analysed transects. Individual transect trends ranged from to meters per year. The analysis processed a total of valid shoreline observations across all transects during the specified period.

The quality of the linear regression models is reflected in an average R² value of , representing the proportion of variance in shoreline position explained by calculated trend.

Comparison

The original analysis, based on the complete temporal record, included transects with an average trend of meters per year (ranging from to meters per year). The time-bounded analysis shows transects with an average trend of meters per year (ranging from to meters per year). This represents a in average trend compared to the historical baseline. Model quality also differs between approaches: the time-bounded analysis achieved an average R² of compared to for the full dataset.

Narrative Generation Configuration

Area of Interest Definitions

The area of interest (AOI) definitions are used to categorise shoreline segments based on their trends and characteristics. Each AOI has a priority, conditions for classification, and a description template for narrative generation. This report returns zones with, at minimum, transects.
